record.paper_title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N
record.original_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain such that every complex geodesic φ: 𝔻 → Ω extends continuously to the closed unit disc, or equivalently continuously up to ∂𝔻. Is that extension property by itself sufficient to force Ω to be visible? Put contrapositively, can there exist a bounded convex domain that is not visible even though every complex geodesic extends continuously to the boundary of the source disc?

evidence.quote: Question 3.7. Does there exist a non-visible bounded convex domain Ω such that every complex geodesic φ : D → Ω extends continuously up to ∂D? In other words, is the continuous extension of all complex geodesics up to the boundary sufficient for visibility?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ be a bounded convex domain. A holomorphic map $\varphi : \mathbb{D} \to \Omega$ (where $\mathbb{D}$ is the open unit disc) is called a complex geodesic if it is an isometry between the Poincaré distance on $\mathbb{D}$ and the Kobayashi distance on $\Omega$. The domain $\Omega$ is said to be visible (in the sense of Bharali–Zimmer) if for every pair of distinct boundary points $p, q \in \partial \Omega$ and every pair of sequences $(x_n), (y_n) \subset \Omega$ with $x_n \to p$ and $y_n \to q$, there exist a compact set $K \subset \Omega$ and Kobayashi almost-geodesics $\sigma_n : [a_n, b_n] \to \Omega$ joining $x_n$ to $y_n$ such that $\sigma_n([a_n, b_n]) \cap K \neq \emptyset$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

Question: Does there exist a bounded convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ that fails to be visible, yet has the property that every complex geodesic $\varphi : \mathbb{D} \to \Omega$ extends continuously to a map $\overline{\mathbb{D}} \to \overline{\Omega}$? Equivalently, is the continuous extension of every complex geodesic up to $\partial \mathbb{D}$ sufficient to imply that $\Omega$ is visible?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the 2025 survey of open questions on visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains. Web search returns no result resolving it; related works (e.g., Bracci–Gaussier–Zimmer, and works on non-visibility of Kobayashi geodesics on C^{1,α} convex domains) give partial geometric characterizations of (non-)visibility but do not establish whether continuous boundary extension of all complex geodesics implies visibility.

status_evidence.title: On non-visibility of Kobayashi geodesics and the geometry of the boundary
status_evidence.snippet: On convex domains with C^{1,α}-smooth boundary, the limit set of non-visible Kobayashi geodesics is contained in a complex face.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial results characterize non-visibility geometrically but do not resolve the question.
